summary: Iteration 5 backend testing for Plan Management CRUD. Added 20 new pytest cases across two classes: TestAdminPlanCatalog (18 cases covering GET /api/plans public, GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/admin/plans with auth gates) and TestUserPlanAssignmentRegression (2 cases verifying PATCH /api/admin/users/{id}/plan still works). ALL 20 new tests pass. Full regression: 99/101 pass. The 2 remaining failures are PRE-EXISTING and unrelated to iter-5 (TestAIMenuFromPhoto: Claude Vision rejects 1x1 PNG fixture; TestOrdersEnhanced.test_order_with_coupon_gst_service: xdist parallel race — both workers mutate the same shared coupon/restaurant state). Verified: seeding of 4 default plans on startup, admin CRUD, 403 for owner, 401 for anon, 400 on missing/duplicate id, 400 on no editable fields, 404 on unknown plan_id, 400 blocking delete of 'free' plan.

critical.issue: PYTHON FUNCTION NAME COLLISION: server.py defines `async def admin_update_plan(...)` TWICE — once at line 1206 for PATCH /api/admin/users/{user_id}/plan and once at line 1252 for PATCH /api/admin/plans/{plan_id}. The main-agent context said this would be renamed to `admin_update_plan_catalog` but it wasn't. FastAPI still registers both routes (decorators run at definition time) so both endpoints work functionally, BUT: (1) OpenAPI schema has duplicate operationId 'admin_update_plan' which breaks auto-generated clients / Swagger UI links; (2) the second definition shadows the first in the module namespace, so any internal import/reference to `admin_update_plan` will get the catalog editor, not the user plan assigner; (3) confusing for maintainers. Rename the second occurrence to `admin_update_plan_catalog` as stated in the plan.

minor.issue: id is silently lowercased (`str(body.get('id','')).strip().lower()`) but no validation on id charset — allows spaces trimmed only from ends, unicode, punctuation. Consider regex ^[a-z0-9_-]{1,32}$ and returning 400 for bad chars.

No validation on `price` (accepts negative, huge floats), `order` (accepts negative), `features` (accepts non-list). float(body.get('price', 0)) will raise 500 (unhandled ValueError) if client sends price='abc' instead of a proper 400. Wrap in try/except and use Pydantic model.
No type/value validation on updates. Admin can PATCH price=-999 or features='not a list' and it will persist. Add Pydantic UpdatePlanCatalogRequest with field validators.

Always returns 200 even when plan_id does not exist (no matched_count check). Returning 200 for a no-op delete is technically idempotent but hides typos. Consider 404 when delete_one().deleted_count==0.

Does NOT check if any users are currently on that plan before deletion. If admin deletes 'premium' while owners have plan='premium', those users are left with a dangling plan reference. Should either block delete (400 'plan in use by N users') or cascade-migrate those users to 'free'.

Since plans are now DB-backed and editable, `/api/plans` returns whatever admin edited. Current DB state has starter=899 (edited from seeded 799) — prev iteration test `TestPlansPricing` asserting exact price 799 was updated to structural check only. Consider a 'reset to defaults' admin endpoint for demo/testing.

Admin plan CRUD uses raw `await request.json()` + dict.get everywhere instead of Pydantic models — no input validation, poor OpenAPI schema, and unhandled float()/int() will bubble as 500 for bad payloads.
DELETE /api/admin/plans returns 200 unconditionally — no `deleted_count` check, no user-reference check. Deleting a plan currently assigned to users leaves dangling references.

GET /api/plans is unauthenticated and returns the raw DB list — good for pricing page, but admin's `order` and internal `_id` (excluded correctly) should not leak. Consider explicit projection whitelist.

Plan seeding only runs when collection is empty. If admin deletes all plans (except free is protected), the seeder will NOT restore them on next boot. Consider `upsert` on id for defaults or a manual /admin/plans/reset endpoint.

rca of the issue: Function name collision RCA: In Python, when two `def foo` share a module, the second binding overrides the first in the namespace. FastAPI's `@api.patch(...)` decorator captures the function object at decoration time and registers the route, so both HTTP endpoints remain functional. However: (a) FastAPI auto-derives `operation_id` from `func.__name__` unless explicitly passed — so /openapi.json will contain TWO operations with `operationId: admin_update_plan`, which violates the OpenAPI spec (operationIds must be unique) and breaks auto-generated Swagger/Redoc clients; (b) if any code inside server.py were to reference `admin_update_plan` by name (e.g., for testing, docs generation, or as a callable), it would resolve to the second (catalog editor) function; (c) it violates the explicit intent stated in the review request. Fix: rename the second function definition at line 1252 to `admin_update_plan_catalog` (per the review request context).
